confidence.A: At least eight years or 32 reported quarters, three attributable material decisions, and an observed adversity period.
confidence.B: Normally five to eight years with a sufficiently attributable operating and capital-allocation record.
confidence.C: Normally three to five years, or an otherwise incomplete or disrupted record.
confidence.D: Under three years, an unlinked leader, or insufficient attributable evidence.

rules: Tenure changes evidence confidence, not the underlying quality score.
Market-price performance is an outcome measure and does not directly award management points.
Inherited conditions must be separated from decisions attributable to the evaluated leader or team.
Every scored component and event modifier must cite point-in-time evidence.
Unverified leadership identities remain unrated rather than receiving a default score.
